Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

Westridge share of Burnaby listings and sales by month

In Westridge, its share of the houses listed in Burnaby went from 2.1% in June to 2.3% in October and its share of the condos and townhomes listed went from 0.1% to 0.5%. A share that holds steady while the city moves means the community is following the city; a share that drifts means it is moving differently.

blocks.text: Westridge home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

9 houses sold in Westridge with a median price of $1,840,000 (the middle half sold between $1,587,000 and $2,980,000), taking a median of 51 days to sell at 92.7% of the last list price; 0% sold above list. They had a median $706 per square foot, a median year built of 1994 and a median lot of 7,208 square feet. 3 townhomes sold in Westridge, too few (5 needed) to give a typical price.

faq.q: How many homes are for sale in Westridge?
faq.a: At the end of October 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 10 houses and 6 condos and townhomes listed in Westridge. Those are month-end counts and they move daily, so ask Jared for a current list.

faq.q: Is Westridge a buyers’ or sellers’ market?
faq.a: In October 2026, houses had a sales ratio of 10% (a buyers’ market); condos and townhomes had 17% on only 6 listed, too few to read as a market type. The sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed; on the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers. One month in one community is a small sample, so look at the monthly table above before you decide.

faq.q: How many homes sold in Westridge from June to October 2026?
faq.a: 4 houses and 2 condos and townhomes sold in Westridge over those 5 months; detached houses peaked in July with 2 sold and condos and townhomes peaked in June with 1 sold.

faq.q: How big is Westridge compared with the rest of Burnaby?
faq.a: In October 2026, Westridge held 2.3% of the 430 detached houses listed in Burnaby and 0.5% of the 1,309 condos and townhomes listed in Burnaby.

faq.q: What mix of houses and condos is for sale in Westridge?
faq.a: In October 2026, houses made up 62.5% of the 16 homes listed in Westridge and condos and townhomes made up 37.5%; of the 2 that sold, houses were 50.0% and condos and townhomes 50.0%.

faq.q: Are there more or fewer homes for sale in Westridge than in June?
faq.a: Listings of detached houses was little changed, 10 in June and 10 in October 2026 (+0.0%); condos and townhomes was 1 in June and 6 in October 2026, too few (under 3) to call a rise or fall.

faq.q: What did houses in Westridge sell for?
faq.a: 9 houses sold in Westridge between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $1,840,000.

faq.q: How long do houses take to sell in Westridge?
faq.a: The median was 51 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 92.7% of the last list price (0% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.
